    (II)   Taxation on dividends

           The Board proposed to distribute a cash dividend for the year 2025 of RMB0.30 per share
           (including tax) with a total amount of RMB4,073,862 thousand based on the total share
           capital of 13,579,541,500 shares of the Company as at 31 December 2025. The above profit
           distribution plan is subject to consideration and approval at the 2025 Annual General Meeting
           of the Company. After being considered and approved, the cash dividend is expected to be
           paid on or before 31 August 2026. The Company will make separate announcements after
           convening of the general meeting in relation to further details of the closure of register of H
           shareholders for distribution of cash dividend and the expected payment date.

           Details of profit distribution of the Company in 2025 are set out in “Section V Corporate
           Governance, Environment and Society (Corporate Governance Report)” of this report.

           In accordance with the relevant regulations on Circular of the State Administration of
           Taxation on Issues Relating to the Withholding and Payment of Enterprise Income Tax on
           Dividends Distributed by PRC Resident Enterprises to Non-resident Enterprise Shareholders
           of Overseas H-shares (Guo Shui Han [2008] No. 897) (《國 家 稅 務 總 局 關 於 中 國 居 民 企 業 向
           境 外H股 非 居 民 企 業 股 東 派 發 股 息 代 扣 代 繳 企 業 所 得 稅 有 關 問 題 的 通 知》(國 稅 函[2008] 897
           號)), when a PRC enterprise distributes annual dividends for the year 2008 and onward to
           their H shareholders who are overseas non-resident enterprises (any H shares registered
           under the name of HKSCC Nominees Limited, other institutional nominees, trustees, or other
           organizations or groups, shall be deemed as shares being held by a non-resident enterprise
           shareholder), enterprise income tax shall be withheld at a uniform rate of 10% by the relevant
           PRC enterprise. Pursuant to the changes in the relevant laws and regulations on taxation in
           the PRC, during the distribution of the dividend of the Company for 2010 and the following
           years, individual shareholders holding the Company’s H shares and listed on the Company’s
           H share register are no longer exempt from personal income tax and are subject to a unified
           withholding tax rate of 10% for enterprise income tax. Meanwhile, in accordance with the
           relevant provisions of the Reply of the State Administration of Taxation on the Collection
           of Enterprise Income Tax on Dividends from Stocks such as B-shares Obtained by Non-
           resident Enterprises (Guo Shui Han [2009] No. 394), non-resident enterprise shareholders
           wishing to enjoy tax treaty benefits shall go through the relevant procedures in accordance
           with the provisions governing the implementation of tax treaties. Non-resident enterprise
           shareholders, after receiving dividends, can apply to the competent tax authority for tax
           treaty (arrangement) treatment through self-declaration or through authorized agents or
           withholding agents. They must provide evidence that they are the actual beneficiaries in
           accordance with the tax treaty (arrangement) provisions. After the competent tax authority
           has verified the information, the difference between the tax already paid and the tax payable
           calculated based on the tax treaty (arrangement) tax rate should be refunded.
82   China Railway Construction Corporation Limited∣Annual Report 2025




       Section IV Management Discussion and Analysis
       (Work Report of the Board of Directors) (continued)


                       In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Notice of the State Administration of
                       Taxation on Issues Concerning the Administration and Collection of Individual Income Tax
                       after the Repeal of Document Guo Shui Fa [1993] No. 045 (Guo Shui Han [2011] No. 348),
                       where a domestic non-foreign-invested enterprise issues shares in Hong Kong, its overseas
                       individual resident shareholders may enjoy relevant preferential tax treatment in accordance
                       with the tax treaties signed between China and the countries of their residence and the
                       tax arrangements between the mainland and Hong Kong (Macao). However, given that the
                       relevant dividend tax rates stipulated in the relevant tax treaties and tax arrangements are
                       generally 10%, and given the large number of shareholders, to simplify tax administration
                       and collection, a domestic non-foreign-invested enterprise issuing shares in Hong Kong
                       may generally withhold and pay individual income tax at a rate of 10% when distributing
                       dividends, without the need for going through application procedures. According to the
                       provisions of the Notice on the Tax Policies Related to the Pilot Program of the Shanghai-
                       Hong Kong Stock Connect (Cai Shui [2014] No. 81) (《關於滬港股票市場交易互聯互通機制
                       試點有關稅收政策的通知》(財稅[2014] 81 號)), for dividends received by domestic individual
                       investors or domestic securities investment funds from investing in H shares listed on the
                       Hong Kong Stock Exchange through Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect, H share companies
                       shall submit an application to the China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation
                       Limited (hereinafter “CSDCC”) for the CSDCC to provide the register of domestic individual
                       investors to the H-share companies, and the H-share companies shall withhold individual
                       income tax at the tax rate of 20%. Such H-share companies will not withhold and pay the
                       income tax of dividends for domestic enterprise investors and those domestic enterprise
                       investors shall report and pay the relevant tax by themselves. According to the provisions
                       of the Notice on the Tax Policies Related to the Pilot Program of the Shenzhen-Hong Kong
                       Stock Connect (Cai Shui [2016] No. 127)《(關於深港股票市場交易互聯互通機制試點有關稅
                       收政策的通知》(財稅[2016] 127 號)), for dividends received by domestic individual investors
                       or domestic securities investment funds from investing in H shares listed on the Hong Kong
                       Stock Exchange through Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect, H share companies shall
                       submit an application to the CSDCC for the CSDCC to provide the register of members
                       of domestic individual investors to the H-share companies, and the H-share companies
                       shall withhold individual income tax at the tax rate of 20%. Such H-share companies will
                       not withhold and pay the income tax of dividends for domestic enterprise investors, and
                       those domestic enterprise investors shall report and pay the relevant tax by themselves.
                       For dividends received by investors (including enterprise and individual investors) in the
                       Hong Kong market from investing in A shares listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, and
                       prior to Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company Ltd. (hereinafter “HKSCC”) being able to
                       furnish the identity, holding period and other detailed data of investors in the Hong Kong
                       market to CSDCC, the differentiated tax treatment based on the holding period of shares will
                       temporarily not be implemented. Listed companies shall withhold income tax at a tax rate of
                       10% and make withholding filings with their competent tax authorities. For those investors
                       who are tax residents of other countries and the tax rate applicable to dividends is lower
                       than 10% under the tax treaty between China and their residence countries, investors may
                       by themselves or ask the withholding agent to act on their behalf to apply to the competent
                       tax authorities of the listed company for preferential treatment under the treaties. With the
                       approval of the competent tax authorities, the difference between the tax withheld and the tax
                       calculated at the rate as prescribed under the corresponding tax treaty shall be refunded.

                       Under the current practice of the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department, no tax is payable
                       in Hong Kong in respect of the dividends paid by the Company.
                                                                                                         83

            (Work Report of the Board of Directors) (continued)


        According to the Notice on Relevant Matters of Differentiated Individual Income Tax Policy
        for Listed Companies’ Dividends (Cai Shui [2015] No. 101) (《關於上市公司股息紅利差別化
        個人所得稅政策有關問題的通知》(財稅[2015] 101號)), if any individual acquires listed shares
        from listed companies in the public issuance and the transfer market and holds such shares
        within 1 month (inclusive), the full amount of his/her dividend income shall be included in
        taxable income; if the individual holds such shares for a period from more than 1 month
        to 1 year (inclusive), 50% of his/her dividend income shall be included in taxable income;
        an individual income tax rate of 20% shall be uniformly applicable to the taxable portion
        of the said income; for shares of listed companies obtained by individuals from the public
        issuance and the transfer market, if any individual holds such shares for more than 1 year, no
        individual income tax will be imposed on the dividend income for the time being.

        IV.     SHAREHOLDER RIGHTS (DISCLOSURE PURSUANT TO THE REQUIREMENTS OF
                THE HONG KONG STOCK EXCHANGE LISTING RULES)

                (I)    Convening an Extraordinary General Meeting by Shareholders

                       According to the provisions of the Articles of Association, a shareholder alone or
                       shareholders together holding at least 10 percent of the Company’s shares shall have the
                       right to make a request to the Board in writing to convene an extraordinary General Meeting.
                       The Board shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations and the provisions of
                       the Articles of Association, give a written response on whether or not it agrees to convene
                       such a meeting within 10 days after receipt of the request. If the Board agrees to convene
                       an extraordinary General Meeting, it shall issue a notice convening such meeting within 5
                       days after it has so resolved. The consent of the relevant shareholder(s) shall be obtained if
                       any change is to be made in the notice to the original request. If the Board does not agree to
                       convene such meeting, or fails to give a response within 10 days after receipt of the request,
                       a shareholder alone or shareholders together holding at least 10 percent of the Company’s
                       shares shall have the right to propose to the Audit and Risk Management Committee in
                       writing to convene the extraordinary General Meeting. If the Audit and Risk Management
                       Committee agrees to convene an extraordinary general meeting, a notice of the general
                       meeting shall be issued within five days after receiving the request. Any changes to the
                       original request in the notice shall be subject to the consent of the relevant shareholders. If
                       the Audit and Risk Management Committee fails to issue the notice of the general meeting
                       within the specified period, it shall be deemed that the Audit and Risk Management
                       Committee does not convene and chair the general meeting. In such case, a shareholder
                       or shareholders holding, individually or collectively, 10% or more of the Company’s shares
                       continuously for 90 days or more may convene and chair the general meeting on their own.

           or collectively more than one percent of the Company’s shares may submit temporary
           proposals in writing to the convener ten days prior to the convening of the General Meeting.
           The convener shall issue a supplementary notice of the General Meeting and make a public
           announcement of the contents of such new resolutions within two days after receipt of the
           proposals, and submit such new proposal(s) to the General Meeting for consideration,
           unless such proposal violates laws, administrative regulations or the Company’s Articles of
           Association, or falls outside the scope of authority of the General Meeting. The notice of the
           General Meeting shall include the following contact information: the date, place and duration
           of the meeting, the time and place for serving the form of proxy appointed for voting at the

                (I)    Overview of the Board

                       The Board is a permanent body of the Company for making business decisions, and shall

                       directors. The Board shall be elected and replaced through election at the General Meeting,

                (IV)   Board diversity policy

                       In order to further enhance the board decision-making efficiency and corporate governance
                       level of the Company, the Company has adopted the board diversity policy, and incorporated
                       it into the duties of the Nomination Committee of the Board in August 2013 and set it out in
                       the “Rules of Work of the Nomination Committee of the Board”. When selecting directors,
                       the Company would give full consideration to the diversity of Board members, including
                       but not limited to the factors of gender, age, region, cultural & education background,
                       professional experience, service term, etc. All appointments by the Board follow the principle
                       of employment by meritocracy, and are eventually decided based on good qualities of
                       candidates and the contributions they could make to the Board.

                       During the Reporting Period, as for the board diversity policy, the Board has adopted and
                       achieved the following measurable targets: at least 1 independent non-executive director
                       shall usually reside in Hong Kong; at least 1 independent non-executive director shall have
                       working experience as financial principal in large enterprises or shall be an expert in the
                       aspect of enterprise finance and accounting; the number of independent non-executive
                       directors shall be no less than one third of the total number of Board members, and the sum
                       of independent non-executive directors and non-executive directors shall exceed half of the
                       number of Board members. In March 2025, the Board added one female worker director,
                       achieving gender diversity of board members.

                (V)    Performance of the duties of corporate governance by the Board

                       In compliance with the regulatory requirements of the stock exchange where the Company
                       is listed, the Board strictly implemented the provisions of the “Rules of Procedure for Board
                       Meetings” in executing corporate governance responsibilities, including but not limited to:
                       formulating and reviewing the Company’s corporate governance policies and practices, and
                       making recommendations. Reviewing and monitoring the training and continuous professional
                       development of directors and senior management. The Board actively arranged directors and
                       senior management to participate in training related to their duties, and communicated with
                       directors and senior management personnel on the updates and changes of regulatory laws
                       and regulations in a timely manner, so that the directors and senior management personnel
                       could sustainably develop their professional competence and improve their capabilities of
                       performance of duties. Reviewing and monitoring the Company’s policies and practices
                       on compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. The Board paid close attention to
                       the compliance of the Company’s operations and established and refined the general legal
                       consultation system. With the establishment of the legal and compliance department and
                       engagement of law firms, the Company was able to comply with the requirements of laws
                       and regulatory regulations. Developing, reviewing and monitoring the code of conduct and
                       compliance manual for employees and directors. Review the Company’s compliance with
                       the relevant corporate governance requirements of the listing rules of the stock exchanges
                       where the shares of the Company are listed and the disclosure in the Corporate Governance
                       Report. The Board required the Company to strictly comply with the relevant corporate
                       governance requirements of the listing rules of the stock exchanges where the shares of the
                       Company are listed, and disclose information related to corporate governance in a timely
                       manner.

VI.   MANAGEMENT (DISCLOSURE PURSUANT TO THE REQUIREMENTS OF THE HONG
      KONG STOCK EXCHANGE LISTING RULES)

      (I)    Overview of the management

             The daily production and operation of the Company is carried out under the president
             accountability system. The Company shall have one president, multiple vice presidents, chief
             accountant, chief engineer, chief economist, general counsel, chief compliance officer and
             safety director, all of which are appointed or dismissed by the Board.

             The president shall be accountable to the Board and exercise the following functions and
             powers: to be in charge of the production, operation and management of the Company and
             to organise the implementation of the resolutions of the Board, and report to the Board; to
             arrange for the implementation of the Company’s annual business plans and investment
             plans; to propose the establishment of the Company’s internal management structure plans;
             to propose the basic management systems of the Company; to formulate the specific rules
             and regulations of the Company; to request the Board to engage or dismiss the Company’s
             vice presidents, chief accountant, chief engineer, chief economist, chief legal advisor,
             chief compliance officer, chief safety officer; to engage or dismiss management personnel
             other than those to be engaged or dismissed by the Board;to exercise other powers and
             authorities conferred by the Board of Directors.

             According to the requirements of the Board, the president shall provide the Board with
             important information about the Company’s operating results, major transactions and material
             contracts, financial condition and business prospects in a timely manner, report his work to
             the Board on a regular basis, and ensure the authenticity, objectivity and completeness of
             such reports.

      (II)   President

             During the Reporting Period, the position of president of the Company was temporarily
             vacant. On 11 February 2026, Mr. PEI Minshan was appointed as the president of the
             Company. He is responsible for the daily operation of the Company, mainly including
             presiding over the Company’s production, operation and management, implementing the
             strategies and policies approved by the Board, the Company’s business plan and investment
             plan, drafting the Company’s internal management structure and basic management system,
             formulating the Company’s specific rules, requesting the Board to engage or dismiss other
             senior management personnel, and exercising other functions and powers granted by the
             Articles of Association and the Board. The president shall be accountable to the Board
             regarding to the Company’s operation conditions, and shall report to the Board regularly.

                 (II)   Nomination Committee

                        The main duties of the Nomination Committee include regulating the selection standards
                        and procedures of the directors, president and other senior management of the Company,
                        implementing and reviewing the policy on Board diversity, etc. Among them, the director
                        nomination policy specifies major standards and principles on the nomination of directors
                        of the Company and the measures to be adopted by the Nomination Committee for the
                        implementation of such policy: 1. to examine the structure, number of members and
                        composition (including professional skills, knowledge and expertise related aspects)
                        of the Board at least once a year and provide recommendations to the Board on any
                        changes proposed to complement the Company’s strategies; 2. to consider the criteria
                        and procedures for the selection of directors and senior management, and provide
                        recommendations thereon to the Board; 3. to widely seek for candidates that have the
                        appropriate qualifications to serve as directors and senior management; 4. to review and
                        make recommendations regarding candidates for directorship and senior management
                        positions; 5. to assess the independence of independent non-executive directors; 6. to
                        make recommendations to the Board on the appointment or re-appointment of directors and
                        senior management, as well as matters related to succession planning for directors and
                        senior management (particularly the Chairman and the President); 7. to report its decisions
                        or recommendations to the Board, except where prohibited by law or regulatory restrictions;
                        8. other matters authorized by the Board; 9. other relevant requirements for the committee’s
                        responsibilities as amended from time to time under the listing rules of the stock exchange
                        where the Company’s shares are listed. When reviewing the scale and composition of the
                        Board and searching for and proposing the candidates for the directors, the Nomination
                        Committee will consider the diversity of the Board from various aspects based on the
                        business mode and specific needs, including but not limited to the gender, age, culture,
                        education background and professional experience. During the Reporting Period, the
                        Nomination Committee strictly followed the above nomination policy.

                        During the Reporting Period, the Nomination Committee performed its duties conscientiously
                        pursuant to the requirements of the Company Law, the Articles of Association, the Terms
                        of Reference of the Nomination Committee and relevant laws and regulations and reviewed
                        the structure, number of members and the composition (including skills, knowledge and
                        experience) of the Board, by way of circulation of relevant documents and other means. The
                        Nomination Committee held a total of 4 meetings during the Reporting Period.

   (V)   Audit and Risk Management Committee

         The responsibilities of the Audit and Risk Management Committee primarily include:
         examining the Company’s compliance with laws and regulations, guiding the construction
         of relevant management systems, and supervising and evaluating the effectiveness of
         the institutional framework; reviewing financial information and its disclosure, deliberating
         on changes to accounting policies and accounting estimates; overseeing internal audit,
         implementing audit plans and rectifications, and studying significant audit conclusions
         and remediation efforts; supervising, evaluating, and communicating with internal and
         external auditors, making recommendations on proposing the appointment, replacement,
         and remuneration for the head of the company’s audit department and external auditors,
         and addressing any matters related to the resignation or dismissal of audit firms; monitoring
         the conduct of directors and senior management in performing their duties; confirming the
         list of connected parties and conducting preliminary reviews of connected transactions;
         researching, analyzing, and assessing risks related to sustainability and ESG matters,
         reviewing reports, and overseeing implementation; and other duties as required by the Board
         and the listing rules.

         During the Reporting Period, in accordance with the requirements of the Company Law,
         the Articles of Association and the Terms of Reference for the Audit and Risk Management
         Committee and other relevant laws and regulations, the Audit and Risk Management
         Committee earnestly performed its duties, jointly reviewed the financial and accounting
         policies, the internal control system, ESG report and relevant financial matters, expressed
         opinions on the appointment of external auditors and listened to the reports of external
         auditors on the audit and review of the 2024 annual report and the 2025 interim report to
         ensure the completeness, fairness and accuracy of the financial statements, reports and
         other relevant data, and established and improved a complete and effective internal control
         system. The Audit and Risk Management Committee held a total of 7 meetings during the
         Reporting Period.

   (II)    Remuneration policy

           ✓   Applicable          Not applicable

           The Company implements a remuneration policy with remuneration budget management,
           and links between remuneration and performance based on the principle of “the better
           performance, the higher remuneration”. The total wages are controlled by three links: benefit
           determination, efficiency adjustment, and level regulation. That is, the growth of total wages
           is linked to the increase in the economic benefits of the enterprise, while making moderate
           adjustments by reference to industry benchmarks’ efficiency levels and taking into account
           the fairness of income distribution to carry out horizontal regulation. And remuneration
           of employees is determined based on performance of the enterprises and that of each
           individual.

           The remuneration of the employees includes wages, performance bonus and allowance.
           The employees of the Company are also entitled to pension insurance, medical insurance,
           unemployment insurance, work injury insurance, maternity insurance and the housing
           provident funds as well as other benefits.

   (III)   Training plan

           ✓   Applicable          Not applicable

           In 2025, the Company’s training initiatives adhered to the overarching principle of seeking
           progress while maintaining stability, with a focus on key areas and comprehensive
           coordination. Efforts were concentrated on implementing various training tasks in
           accordance with the annual training plan. Upholding the principles of “categorization and
           grading, training all who should be trained, and precise scheduling”, a blended approach
           combining online and offline methods was adopted. The company continued to intensify
           employee training efforts, further enhancing the training participation rate among staff. The
           training rate for senior management and middle-level management personnel reached 100%,
           and the training rate for general employees reached more than 96%, with an average study
           time of more than 90 hours. Throughout the year, the Company had a total of 1,451,097
           attendances in the trainings, including 551,138 offline attendances and 899,959 online
           attendances. Among them, the attendances reached 32,837 in training enterprise leaders,
           196,849 in training operation management personnel, 980,716 in training professional and
           technical personnel, 68,929 in training party and mass management personnel, and 171,766
           training skilled personnel. First, in-depth study and joint training on “Xi Jinping’s Selected
           Works on Economy” Volume I were carried out. Second, we organized training programs
           such as the “Middle-aged and Young Cadres Leadership Enhancement Training Class,”
           the “Newly Appointed Leaders of Secondary and Tertiary Units Training Class,” the “2025
           Spring Semester Cadre Advanced Studies Class,” and the “Chief Engineer Training Class”
           to enhance the performance capabilities of leaders at all levels. Thirdly, we continued to
           strengthen the training of overseas talent teams. By adopting the “online + offline” methods,
           we held a training course for overseas senior managers at Tianjin University; conducted
           training on 5 languages across 7 classes by the “online” teaching method at Beijing Foreign
           Studies University, and 360 domestic and foreign employees participated in the study in
           2025. Fourth, we strengthened the development of skilled talent teams. We conducted skills
           training for engineering budget officers, on-site professionals in the housing and urban-rural
           development sector, BIM application technology, shield machine and special equipment
           operators, and drone pilots, continuously improving the quality and operational proficiency of
           various skilled personnel; we organized training classes for quality supervisors and assessors
           in skilled talent evaluation and qualification certification; we carried out senior technician
           evaluations, with 179 individuals obtaining senior technician qualifications.

XIII. PROFIT DISTRIBUTION PLAN OR RESERVE-TO-EQUITY

    (I)    The profit distribution policies of the Company (disclosure pursuant to the
           requirements of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange Listing Rules)

           1.    The basic principles of the profit distribution policies of the Company

                 The Company shall take full account of the return to investors and distribute dividends
                 to shareholders on a yearly basis in a specific proportion out of the distributable profit
                 realised for the year as set out in that year’s consolidated financial statements. The
                 profit distribution policies of the Company shall maintain continuity and stability while
                 giving consideration to the interests of the Company in the long term, the interests of
                 all shareholders as a whole, and the sustainable development of the Company. The
                 Company shall distribute its profit by way of cash dividends as priority.

           2.    The specific profit distribution policies of the Company

                 (1)   Form of profit distribution

                        The Company may distribute dividends in cash, in shares or in a combination
                        of both cash and shares. Under favourable circumstances, the Company may
                        distribute interim dividends.
128   China Railway Construction Corporation Limited∣Annual Report 2025




        Section V Corporate Governance, Environment and Society
        (Corporate Governance Report) (continued)


                               (2)     Specific conditions, proportions and intervals of cash dividends of the Company

                                       In the absence of certain special circumstances, if the Company’s profit for the
                                       year and its total undistributed profit is positive, the Company shall distribute
                                       dividends in cash and such profit to be distributed in cash on a yearly basis
                                       must not be less than 15% of the distributable profit to ordinary shareholders
                                       realised for the year as set out in that year’s consolidated financial statements.

                                       Such special circumstances refer to the following: a. where the audit firm issues
                                       a non-standard unqualified audit report for the financial report of the Company
                                       for that financial year; and b. where the Company has major investment plan or
                                       significant cash expenditure, excluding projects funded by raised proceeds.

                                       Such major investment plan or significant cash expenditure refers to the
                                       external investment and asset acquisition by the Company with accumulated
                                       expenditure within the following 12 months amounting to or exceeding 30% of
                                       the latest audited net assets.

                                       When the aforesaid conditions of cash distribution are met, cash dividends
                                       shall be distributed once a year in principle. The Board of Directors of the
                                       Company can propose a distribution of interim cash dividends according to the
                                       Company’s situation of profitability and capital needs.

                               (3)     Specific conditions for distributing dividends in shares by the Company

                                       When the Company is operating well and the Board considers that the share
                                       price of the Company does not reflect its scale of share capital and the
                                       distribution of dividends in shares is in the interests of all shareholders of the
                                       Company, the Company may propose the distribution plan of dividends in
                                       shares upon fulfilment of the above conditions concerning cash dividends.

   (II)   Formulation, implementation or adjustment of the cash dividend policy

          ✓    Applicable        Not applicable

          1.    Details of implementation of the cash dividend policy during the Reporting Period

                Pursuant to the resolution of the 37th Meeting of the 5th Session of the Board of
                Directors held by the Company on 27 March 2025, for the year 2025, a cash dividend
                of RMB3.00 per 10 shares (including tax) was proposed based on the total share
                capital of 13,579,541,500 shares as at 31 December 2024, with a total cash dividend
                distribution of RMB4,073,862 thousand. This profit distribution plan was considered
                and approved at the 2024 Annual General Meeting of the Company held on 20 June
                2025. The above cash dividends were fully paid on 22 July 2025 and 14 August 2025
                respectively.

          2.    Formulation, implementation or adjustment of the cash dividend policy

                During the Reporting Period, while maintaining sustainable and stable development,
                the Company highly valued reasonable investment return to its shareholders.
                According to relevant regulations by the CSRC and the Articles of Association, the
                approval procedure for the cash dividend distribution policy and profit distribution
                policy was clearly defined. The Company’s profit distribution policy is in compliance
                with the Articles of Association and review process requirements. The standard and
                proportion of dividends are clear, and the relevant decision-making mechanism and
                procedures are complete. The Independent Directors of the Company fulfilled their
                responsibilities with due diligence, carefully reviewed the cash dividend policy and
                issued independent opinions. The Company has adopted a number of ways for small
                and medium-sized shareholders to fully express their views and demands, and fully
                safeguarded the legitimate rights and interests of minority shareholders.

                To facilitate investors to have a more comprehensive and in-depth understanding
                of the specific details of the Company’s cash dividend distribution for the year
                2024, the Company held a cash dividend briefing via online means on 1 April 2025,
                and answered questions on cash dividends widely concerned by investors. On 20
                June 2025, the Company held the 2024 Annual General Meeting by way of on-site
                registered voting combined with online voting, and considered and approved the
                Proposal on the Company’s Profit Distribution Plan for the Year 2024.

                        3.     Explanation on profit distribution plan for 2025

                               (1)     The 2025 profit distribution plan approved by the Board

                                       In accordance with the Company’s audited financial report for 2025, the
                                       undistributed profit of the parent company at the beginning of 2025 was
                                       RMB51,364,222 thousand. Adding the net profit of the parent company for
                                       the current year of RMB11,800,955 thousand, deducting cash dividends for
                                       2024 of RMB4,073,862 thousand and interest distributed to holders of other
                                       equity instruments for 2025 of RMB2,389,779 thousand, the distributable profit
                                       of the parent company at the end of the year amounted to RMB56,701,536
                                       thousand. Pursuant to the Company Law and the Articles of Association, based
                                       on the total share capital of the Company of 13,579,541,500 shares as at 31
                                       December 2025, a cash dividend of RMB3.00 per 10 shares (tax inclusive) is
                                       proposed, representing a total profit distribution of RMB4,073,862 thousand,
                                       accounting for 25.50% of the distributable profit attributable to ordinary
                                       shareholders of the listed company in the consolidated financial statements
                                       for the year. After distribution, the remaining undistributed profit of the parent
                                       company of RMB52,627,674 thousand will be carried forward to the next year.
                                       If the Company’s total share capital changes before the record date for the
                                       implementation of the equity distribution, the Company intends to maintain the
                                       total distribution amount unchanged and adjust the per-share distribution ratio
                                       accordingly.

                               (2)     The time arrangement of the profit distribution plan for 2025

                                       The Company’s 2025 profit distribution proposal is subject to review and
                                       approval at the Company’s 2025 Annual General Meeting. Upon approval of the
                                       dividend proposal at the Company’s 2025 Annual General Meeting (the date of
                                       which is yet to be determined and will be announced by the Company in due
                                       course), the proposed dividend is expected to be distributed to the Company’s
                                       shareholders on or before 31 August 2026. Any changes to the expected
                                       distribution date will be announced by the Company in due course.

                               (3)     Board of Directors’ Explanation on the Company’s 2025 Profit Distribution
                                       Proposal

                                       ①       Industry Conditions and Characteristics

                                              The construction industry in which the Company operates is a fully
                                              competitive industry, characterized by large individual project volumes,
                                              long production cycles, relatively high accounts receivable and
                                              inventory, and substantial demand for working capital in daily operations.
                                              In 2025, fixed-asset investment in traditional sectors in China such as
                                              highways, municipal works and housing construction declined somewhat,
                                              while emerging markets including power engineering and mining
                                              engineering achieved leapfrog development. The construction industry is
                                              undergoing structural adjustment. Such changes bring both challenges
                                              and opportunities, opening up new growth space for enterprises with
                                              technological reserves and qualification advantages.
                                                                                               131




Section V Corporate Governance, Environment and Society
              (Corporate Governance Report) (continued)


             ②   Company Development Stage and Business Model

                 The Company is currently at a critical stage of transformation from scale
                 expansion to high-quality development. It will continue to consolidate
                 its advantages in the traditional infrastructure market while accelerating
                 the deployment of new growth drivers. By strengthening investment in
                 innovative R&D and qualification acquisition in green and low-carbon,
                 underground space, high-end equipment, new materials, new energy,
                 bamboo-based industry, marine economy and other fields, the Company
                 will promote the intelligent and green transformation of traditional
                 industries.

             ③   Profitability, Solvency and Capital Requirements

                 In recent years, the Company has maintained relatively stable
                 profitability and generated sustained and stable investment returns for
                 shareholders. First of all, the Company will reasonably arrange fund
                 expenditures in accordance with its business development needs, further
                 optimize the use of funds, coordinate fund allocation and improve fund
                 utilization efficiency, so as to support the sound, stable and sustainable
                 development of the Company. On the one hand, the Company needs to
                 maintain sufficient funds to meet the liquidity needs of daily operations;
                 on the other hand, capital investment is required for the Company to
                 foster strategic emerging industries, expand emerging businesses and
                 intensify scientific and technological innovation. Meanwhile, retaining a
                 certain proportion of retained earnings helps enhance the Company’s
                 risk resilience and support its sustainable development.

             ④   Use of Retained Earnings and Expected Returns

                 The retained undistributed profits of the Company will be used to
                 seize development opportunities, promote the transformation and
                 upgrading of traditional industries, support the development of strategic
                 emerging industries and conduct innovative technology research. The
                 Company will adhere to the general principle of pursuing progress while
                 maintaining stability, accelerate consolidation and upgrading, innovation
                 and cultivation, as well as quality and efficiency improvement, enhance
                 efficiency and effectiveness, strengthen core competitiveness, and bring
                 long-term and stable returns to shareholders. In the past three years,
                 the Company’s dividend payout ratio has remained above 20% and has
                 been steadily increasing, maintaining a stable dividend distribution level.

         XV.     CONSTRUCTION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM DURING
                 THE REPORTING PERIOD
                 ✓       Applicable         Not applicable

                 CRCC has attached great importance to the construction and implementation of the internal control
                 system. During the Reporting Period, the Company further improved the supporting systems
                 related to internal controls. It issued the “Regulations Management Measures” to strengthen the
                 full lifecycle management of regulations–from drafting, approval, and issuance to revision and
                 abolition–at the source. The “Organization Management Measures” were issued to standardize
                 the establishment of organizational structures, strengthen organizational management, and
                 enhance organizational efficiency. The “Staffing Management Measures” were issued to regulate
                 personnel quota management across all levels, reasonably allocate and fully utilize human
                 resources, and improve personnel efficiency. The “Authorization and Delegation Management
                 Measures for Secondary Companies” were issued to strengthen the management of authorizations
                 and delegations to secondary companies, implement the authority of the boards of directors
                 of secondary companies, and enhance corporate governance effectiveness. The “Total Wage
                 Management Measures” were issued to strengthen and improve compensation management, refine
                 wage determination and normal growth mechanisms, and stimulate vitality. The “Remuneration
                 Management Measures for Subsidiary Heads” were issued to standardize the management
                 of remuneration income for subsidiary heads, improve incentive and restraint mechanisms,
                 promote better operating performance of subsidiaries, and enhance development quality. The
                 “Headquarters Budget Management Measures” were issued to standardize headquarters budget
                 management, clarify responsibilities, optimize resource allocation, and improve refinement levels.
                 The “Headquarters Expenditure Management Measures” were issued to regulate headquarters
                 expenditure management, clarify management responsibilities, expenditure standards, approval
                 authorities, and payment processes, ensuring efficient and compliant funds management. The “2025
                 Internal Control Supervision and Evaluation Implementation Plan” was issued, and a consulting firm
                 was engaged to conduct internal control supervision and evaluation for fourteen units. Adopting a
                 problem-oriented approach and adhering to the principle of “tracing from the source and focusing
                 on typical cases,” the Company comprehensively reviewed the implementation of internal controls.
                                                                                                              135




Section V Corporate Governance, Environment and Society
              (Corporate Governance Report) (continued)

XVI. MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL OF SUBSIDIARIES DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD

    ✓    Applicable          Not applicable

    During the Reporting Period, CRCC comprehensively implemented lean management in terms
    of organisation, operation, and projects. It has built a basic management system that is oriented
    towards value creation, focused on management improvement, and aimed at improving its
    development quality and efficiency. Strengthening institutional development, the Company issued
    the “China Railway Construction Corporation Limited Institutional Management Measures,” further
    clarifying the positioning and responsibility boundaries of business institutions at all levels.
    This established a systematic, well-defined, scientifically standardized, and orderly operational
    organizational control system, enhancing management efficiency and value creation capabilities.
    The Company strengthened source control by establishing a joint review system for newly
    established entities. The Company required all newly established entities to be submitted to the
    Group for approval or filing, and subject to joint review of strategic necessity, economic feasibility,
    risk controllability, and plan rationality. The Company implemented an early warning mechanism
    for legal entities, conducted tracking, evaluation, and label management for newly established
    companies. Green indicates normal development, yellow triggers diagnostic rectification, and
    red leads to downsizing or liquidation, so as to improve the monitoring system for functional
    subsidiaries. The Company conducted a comprehensive annual operational assessment of
    functional subsidiaries, systematically collected data, conducted in-depth analysis and evaluation,
    issued a thematic circular to highlight major issues, and made specific arrangements regarding
    the direction of rectification, responsibility assignment, and timeline requirements, thereby
    strengthening whole-process supervision and ensuring the formation of a closed-loop operational
    control mechanism.

    Risk warning regarding abnormal management control over subsidiaries

                 (V)     Employee gender diversity

                         The Company strictly complies with the Labour Law of the People’s Republic of China,
                         the Labour Contract Law of the People’s Republic of China and other relevant laws and
                         regulations, to regulate the employment practices and protect the legitimate rights and
                         interests of its employees. The Company always follows the principle of equal employment
                         and adheres to a policy of equal pay for equal work and non-discrimination in labour
                         employment. It provides equal employment opportunities for employees of different
                         nationalities, races, genders, ages, religious beliefs, and cultural backgrounds. As at the
                         end of the Reporting Period, the ratio of male employees to female employees (including
                         senior management) of the Company was 3.88:1. The Company will continue to implement
                         measures that support employee diversity during recruitment.

                 (VI)    Amendments to the Articles of Association during the Reporting Period

                         During the Reporting Period, in accordance with the requirements of relevant laws and
                         regulations of the stock exchange where the Company’s shares are listed and the Company’s
                         actual circumstances, the Articles of Association were amended once following review and
                         approval by the Board and the General Meeting.

                         In order to implement the new Company Law and in accordance with the relevant regulatory
                         requirements of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the State-owned Assets
                         Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council, and the stock exchanges
                         where the Company is listed, the Company has revised its Articles of Association and
                         its appendices, namely the Rules of Procedure for General Meeting and the Rules of
                         Procedure for Board Meeting, and abolished the Board of Supervisors, based on its actual
                         circumstances. These revisions were approved by the Company’s 2024 Annual General
                         Meeting held on 20 June 2025. The revised Articles of Association, Rules of Procedure for
                         General Meeting, and Rules of Procedure for Board Meeting were published on 21 June
                         2025, on the website of the Shanghai Stock Exchange (www.sse.com.cn), the website of
                         The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (www.hkex.com.hk), and the Company’s website
                         (www.crcc.cn).

                 (I)     Information in relation to the review on the financial statements by the Audit and Risk
                         Management Committee

                         In accordance with the Terms of Reference of the Audit and Risk Management Committee
                         of the Board of China Railway Construction Corporation Limited and the regulatory
                         requirements, during the Reporting Period, the Audit and Risk Management Committee
                         actively supervised and evaluated the work of the external auditors. The Committee provided
                         timely and effective supervision and evaluation throughout the planning, progress, and
                         concluding stages of the annual audit conducted by the accounting firm, earnestly carried
                         out the review of the Company’s annual and interim reports, and provided professional
                         advice and suggestions on the preparation of periodic reports.

                         The schedule on the review of the Company’s annual financial report was negotiated and
                         determined by the Audit and Risk Management Committee of the Board with the accounting
                         firm for annual audit. Before the accounting firm for annual audit officially started the audit,
                         the Audit and Risk Management Committee reviewed the annual financial statements
                         prepared by the Company, and formed a written opinion. After the accounting firm for
                         annual audit started the audit, the Audit and Risk Management Committee strengthened
                         communication with the accounting firm for annual audit. After the accounting firm for annual
                         audit issued the preliminarily audit opinion, the Audit and Risk Management Committee once
                         again reviewed the Company’s annual financial statements and formed a written opinion. The
                         Audit and Risk Management Committee voted on the annual financial statements, formed a
                         resolution and submitted it to the Board for review. The financial statements of the Company
                         for the year ended 31 December 2025 were reviewed by the Audit and Risk Management
                         Committee of the sixth session of the Board at its 7th Meeting on 29 March 2026.

                 Explanation on appointment and removal of auditors

                  ✔ Applicable              Not Applicable

                 1.     Pursuant to relevant requirements of the Ministry of Finance, the CSRC and the Hong Kong
                        Stock Exchange, a company incorporated in Mainland China and listed on the Hong Kong
                        Stock Exchange is permitted to adopt the PRC GAAP Standards to prepare its financial
                        statements and to engage a domestic accounting firm recognised by the Ministry of Finance
                        and the CSRC to provide relevant services in accordance with the PRC auditing standards
                        since 15 December 2010. Therefore, the Company appointed only one auditor as its external
                        auditor starting from the financial year of 2011, with no division of domestic and overseas.

                 2.     In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Administrative Measures for the Selection
                        and Appointment of Accounting Firms by State-owned Enterprises and Listed Companies
                        (Cai Kuai [2023] No. 4) jointly issued by the Ministry of Finance, the State-owned Assets
                        Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council (SASAC) and the CSRC,
                        and the Working Rules for the Administration of Financial Final Accounts Audit of Central
                        Enterprises (Guo Zi Fa Cai Ping Gui [2024] No. 20) issued by SASAC, an accounting firm
                        shall not continuously undertake the financial final accounts audit business of the same
                        enterprise for more than 8 years. From 2017 to 2024, the Company appointed Deloitte
                        Touche Tohmatsu Certified Public Accountants LLP as the external auditor of the Company
                        for eight consecutive years, which was required to be replaced in accordance with the
                        aforesaid provisions. As considered and approved at the 2024 Annual General Meeting of
                        the Company on 20 June 2025, the Company appointed Ernst & Young Hua Ming LLP as
                        the audit intermediary service institution of the Company for 2025, with a total audit fee of
                        RMB25.00 million (of which RMB23.30 million was for the audit of the 2025 domestic and
                        overseas financial statements and the review of the 2025 interim financial statements, and
                        RMB1.70 million was for the audit of the 2025 internal control).

                 3.     In accordance with Article 20ZT of the Hong Kong Financial Reporting Council Ordinance
                        (Cap. 588), Ernst & Young Hua Ming LLP is an eligible external audit firm.

2.   Continuing connected transaction under the Property Leasing Framework
     Agreement and its supplementary agreement between the Company and the
     Controlling Shareholder

     The Company entered into the Property Leasing Framework Agreement (as
     supplemented by a supplemental agreement dated 28 December 2012)
     with the Controlling Shareholder on 5 November 2007, for a term of 10 years
     commencing on 5 November 2007. The principal terms of the Property Leasing
     Framework Agreement are that the Controlling Shareholder and/or its connected
     persons/associates agree to lease certain of their lawfully owned properties
     (hereinafter referred to as the “Leased Properties”) to the Company and/or
     its subsidiaries in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Property
     Leasing Framework Agreement; and the Company and/or its subsidiaries agree
     to pay the corresponding consideration to them for the lease of the Leased
     Properties in accordance with the provisions of the Property Leasing Framework
     Agreement.

     The aforesaid Property Leasing Framework Agreement (as supplemented by
     a supplemental agreement dated 28 December 2012) was renewed on 30
     October 2017, 18 December 2019, 28 October 2022, 30 October 2023, 27
     December 2024 and 30 October 2025. Given that the framework agreement
     entered into by the Company and the Controlling Shareholder on 27 December
     2024 and the annual caps determined for the connected transactions
     thereunder both expired on 31 December 2025, in order to facilitate the
     regulation of the continuing connected transactions in respect of the Group’s
     from time to time leasing of properties from the Controlling Shareholder and/or
     its connected persons/associates, on 30 October 2025, the Company renewed
     the framework agreement with the Controlling Shareholder on the same terms,
     for a term from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026, and set the annual cap
     for the continuing connected transactions thereunder for the year ending 31
     December 2026. In setting the 2026 annual caps under the Property Leasing
     Framework Agreement and the Land Use Rights Leasing Framework Agreement,
     the Company has considered: (1) The historical transaction amounts for
     2023, 2024 and 2025 were approximately RMB134 million, RMB136 million
     and RMB152 million respectively; (2) The quotation results obtained by China
     Beijing Equity Exchange for the principal leased properties under the Property
     Leasing Framework Agreement, with reference to the locations of the relevant
     properties, the leasing status of surrounding properties and the historical trend
     of rental prices; (3) In addition to the existing leases of properties and land
     use rights, taking into account the Group’s business development needs, the
     Group is expected to have additional leasing demand for properties and land
     use rights provided by the Controlling Shareholder, and after factoring in the
     reserved buffer space, the annual cap for 2026 is set at RMB200 million.

Loan Services: Subject to compliance with relevant national laws and
regulations, CRCCFC shall provide loan services to the controlling shareholder
and its subsidiaries to meet their operational and development needs. The
controlling shareholder and its subsidiaries shall pay loan interest to CRCCFC
at an interest rate not lower than the applicable interest rate for the same type
of loans in the same period offered by major domestic commercial banks.
During the valid term of the agreement, the daily outstanding balance of loans
obtained by the controlling shareholder and its subsidiaries from CRCCFC shall
not exceed RMB4 billion, and the annual interest shall not exceed RMB144
million.

Clearing Services: CRCCFC shall provide collection and payment services
and other auxiliary services related to settlement business to the Controlling
Shareholder and its subsidiaries in accordance with the instructions of the
Controlling Shareholder. CRCCFC shall charge fees at a rate no lower than the
fee scale of ordinary commercial banks, and the annual service fees shall not
exceed RMB10 million.

Other Financial Services: CRCCFC shall provide other financial services within
its business scope to the controlling shareholder and its subsidiaries at their
request and subject to its own conditions and on the premise of compliance
with the financial service agreement. Fees charged by CRCCFC for other
financial services shall comply with the fee standards stipulated by the People’s
Bank of China or the National Administration of Financial Regulation for such
services, and shall not be lower than the fee standards of major Chinese
financial institutions for similar services. The annual service fee shall not exceed
RMB10 million.

The Company has adopted the following internal control and corporate
governance measures to ensure that the pricing and terms of the continuing
connected transactions are fair and reasonable and no less favourable than
those offered by independent third parties from time to time:

(1)   The Company has formulated a series of internal rules and policies
      relating to the management and control of related (connected)
      transactions, including a decision-making system for connected
      transactions;

(2)   The Company will regularly collect and refer to quotations for similar
      transactions from independent third parties and conduct market
      research on pricing to assess and review whether the prices offered by
      the Controlling Shareholder are fair and reasonable. For transactions
      under the Land Use Right Lease Framework Agreement, the Company
      will determine the market rates with reference to (i) quotations from at
      least two independent third parties for land of similar scale, in the same
      region and under normal trading conditions; (ii) quotations from the
      Controlling Shareholder to independent third parties for similar land;
      (iii) the Company will comprehensively consider the construction area,
      decoration and facilities, geographical location, usage and nature of
      the relevant land, etc., to assess the fairness and reasonableness of
      the quotations offered by the Controlling Shareholder. For transactions
      under the Service Provision Framework Agreement, where there is no
      relevant market price, the transaction price will be determined based on
      the market comparable cost plus gross profit method. The gross profit
      will be determined with reference to the prevailing profit margin, i.e., the
      comparable market profit margin for the relevant services. The Group will
      collect quotations from independent third parties at least monthly and
      conduct market price research through independent industry information
      providers (such as industry websites) to obtain the prevailing profit
      margin.

(3)   Based on the aforesaid framework agreements for continuing connected
      transactions, the Company and its subsidiaries will enter into specific
      agreements with the Controlling Shareholder and/or its related parties/
      associates in respect of the specific requirements of the relevant
      transactions and in accordance with the terms of the framework
      agreements (including the pricing policy), which will be reviewed by the
      relevant business and legal departments.

(4)   The Company’s external auditors will conduct interim reviews and annual
      audits every year, and express opinions on the implementation of the
      pricing policies and whether the actual transaction amounts incurred are
      within the relevant annual caps for the respective year pursuant to the
      Listing Rules of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited.

Based on the above, the Company has established adequate internal control
measures to ensure that the terms of the connected transactions are fair and
reasonable, on normal commercial terms, and in the interests of the Company
and its shareholders as a whole.

2.   Non-Exempt One-Off Connected Transactions

     On 18 December 2019, the Company entered into separate investment agreements
     with eight investors, namely Taiping Life Insurance Co., Ltd. (“Taiping Life”), Beijing
     Chengtong Gongrong Equity Investment Fund (Limited Partnership) (“Chengtong
     Gongrong Fund” ), BOCOM Financial Assets Investment Co., Ltd. (“ BOCOM
     Investment”), Everbright Jinou Asset Management Co., Ltd. (“Everbright Jinou”),
     BOC Financial Assets Investment Co., Ltd. (“BOC Assets”), ABC Financial Assets
     Investment Co., Ltd. (“ABC Investment”), CCB Financial Assets Investment Co.,
     Ltd. (“CCB Investment”) and Shenzhen Xinmaisui Investment Management Co.,
     Ltd. (“Xinmaisui Investment”). Pursuant to which, the investors agreed to subscribe
     for cash capital contributions to China Railway 11th Bureau Group Co., Ltd., China
     Railway Construction Group Co., Ltd., China Railway Construction Investment Group
     Co., Ltd. and China Railway Construction Kunlun Investment Group Co., Ltd. (the
     “Target Companies”) on the terms and conditions of the respective investment
     agreements, with an aggregate capital increase amount of RMB11 billion. Upon
     completion of such capital increases, the Target Companies remained subsidiaries of
     the Company, and the Company retained actual control over the Target Companies.

     On 31 October 2025, the Company entered into separate equity transfer agreements
     with the eight investors: Taiping Life, Chengtong Gongrong Fund, BOCOM
     Investment, Everbright Jinou, BOC Assets, ABC Investment, CCB Investment and
     Xinmaisui Investment, pursuant to which, the Company agreed to acquire from the
     eight investors all their held equity interests in the Target Companies on the terms
     and conditions of the respective equity transfer agreements, including acquiring
     approximately 18.38%, 14.36%, 12.66% and 29.23% equity interests in China Railway
     11th Bureau Group Co., Ltd., China Railway Construction Group Co., Ltd., China
     Railway Construction Investment Group Co., Ltd. and China Railway Construction
     Kunlun Investment Group Co., Ltd. for considerations of RMB2,800 million, RMB2,000
     million, RMB3,200 million and RMB3,000 million respectively. The aggregate cash
     consideration for the aforesaid acquisition is RMB11 billion (the “Acquisition”). Upon
     completion of the Acquisition, the Target Companies will become wholly-owned
     subsidiaries of the Company.

     As at 31 October 2025, Taiping Life held 10.86% equity interest in China Railway 11th
     Bureau Group Co., Ltd. and 17.27% equity interest in China Railway Construction
     Kunlun Investment Group Co., Ltd., and therefore constitutes a substantial shareholder
     of such two subsidiaries. BOC Assets held 11.82% equity interest in China Railway
     18th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. and 14.80% equity interest in China Railway 20th Bureau
     Group Co., Ltd., and therefore constitutes a substantial shareholder of such two
     subsidiaries. Accordingly, under Chapter 14A of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange
     Listing Rules, Taiping Life and BOC Assets are connected persons of the Company at
     the subsidiary level. The acquisition of equity interests in the Target Companies by the
     Company from Taiping Life and BOC Assets constitutes connected transactions of the
     Company.

     Since (i) Taiping Life and BOC Assets are connected persons the Company at
     the subsidiary level; (ii) the highest applicable percentage ratio calculated on a
     combined basis for the acquisition of equity interests in the Target Companies by
     the Company from Taiping Life and BOC Assets exceeds 5%; (iii) the Acquisition
     has been approved by the Board; and (iv) the Directors (including independent non-
     executive Directors) have confirmed that the terms of the Acquisition are fair and
     reasonable, the Acquisition was entered into on normal commercial terms and is in the
     overall interests of the Company and its shareholders, the Acquisition is subject to the
     reporting and announcement requirements but exempt from the circular, independent
     financial advice and shareholders’ approval requirements pursuant to Rule 14A.101 of
     the Hong Kong Stock Exchange Listing Rules.

XVIII. SIGNIFICANT EVENTS AFTER THE REPORTING PERIOD

    (I)    Changes of Directors and Senior Management of the Company

           On 9 January 2026, the Board of the Company received the resignation letter from Mr. Zhao
           Diandong, vice president of the Company. Mr. Zhao Diandong tendered his resignation as
           vice president of the Company due to work reassignment. Following his resignation, Mr.
           Zhao Diandong no longer holds any position within the Company. For details, please refer
           to the relevant announcements published by the Company dated 10 January 2025 on China
           Securities Journal, Shanghai Securities News, Securities Daily, Securities Times and the
           website of Shanghai Stock Exchange (www.sse.com.cn), the website of Hong Kong Stock
           Exchange (www.hkex.com.hk) and the website of the Company (www.crcc.cn).

           On 21 January 2026, the Company convened the Sixth Meeting of the Sixth Session of the
           Board, which reviewed and approved the Proposal on the Appointment of Mr. Sun Liqiang
           as Vice President of the Company and the Cessation of Mr. Chen Zhiming as Vice President
           of the Company. Mr. Sun Liqiang was appointed as Vice President of the Company, with
           his term commencing from the date of approval by the Board, aligning with the tenure of
           the Company’s current senior management. Mr. Chen Zhiming ceased to serve as Vice
           President of the Company due to work adjustment. For details, please refer to the relevant
           announcements published by the Company dated 22 January 2025 on China Securities
           Journal, Shanghai Securities News, Securities Daily, Securities Times and the website of
           Shanghai Stock Exchange (www.sse.com.cn), the website of Hong Kong Stock Exchange
           (www.hkex.com.hk) and the website of the Company (www.crcc.cn).

           On 11 February 2026, the Company convened the seventh meeting of the sixth session of
           the Board, at which the Proposal on the Appointment of Mr. Pei Minshan as President of the
           Company was considered and approved. Mr. Pei Minshan was appointed as the President
           of the Company, with his term commencing from the date of approval by the Board and
           aligning with the tenure of the Company’s current senior management. For details, please
           refer to the relevant announcements published by the Company dated 12 February 2025 on
           China Securities Journal, Shanghai Securities News, Securities Daily, Securities Times and
           the website of Shanghai Stock Exchange (www.sse.com.cn), the website of Hong Kong Stock
           Exchange (www.hkex.com.hk) and the website of the Company (www.crcc.cn).

           On 30 March 2026, the Company convened the 2026 first extraordinary shareholders’
           meeting, at which the Proposal on the Appointment of Additional Executive Directors of
           the Company was considered and approved. Mr. Pei Minshan and Mr. Chen Zhiming were
           appointed as executive directors of the sixth session of the Board. For details, please refer
           to the relevant announcements published by the Company dated 21 March 2026 on China
           Securities Journal, Shanghai Securities News, Securities Daily, Securities Times and the
           website of Shanghai Stock Exchange (www.sse.com.cn), the website of Hong Kong Stock
           Exchange (www.hkex.com.hk) and the website of the Company (www.crcc.cn).

                                                                      Auditor’ s Report

                                                 Ernst & Young Hua Ming [2026] Shen Zi No. 70629682_A01

                                                             China Railway Construction Corporation Limited

To all shareholders of China Railway Construction Corporation Limited

(I)     OPINION

        We have audited the financial statements of China Railway Construction Corporation Limited (the
        “Company”), which comprise the consolidated and company statements of financial position as
        at 31 December 2025, and the consolidated and company statements of profit or loss and other
        comprehensive income, the consolidated and company statements of changes in equity and the
        consolidated and company statements of cash flows for the year then ended, and notes to the
        financial statements.

        In our opinion, the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the
        consolidated and the Company’s financial position as at 31 December 2025, and the consolidated
        and the Company’s financial performance and cash flows for the year then ended in accordance
        with Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (“ASBEs”).

(II)    BASIS FOR OPINION

        We conducted our audit in accordance with China Standards on Auditing (“CSAs”). Our
        responsibilities under those standards are further described in the Auditor’s responsibilities for
        the audit of the financial statements section of our report. We are independent of the Company
        in accordance with China Independence Standard No. 1 – Independence Requirements for
        Financial Statement Audit and Review Engagements and China Code of Ethics for Certified Public
        Accountants (the “Code”), as applicable to audits of financial statements of public interest entities.
        We have also fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with the Code. We believe
        that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our
        opinion.

(III)   KEY AUDIT MATTERS

        Key audit matters are those matters that, in our professional judgement, were of most significance
        in our audit of the financial statements of the current period. These matters were addressed in the
        context of our audit of the financial statements as a whole, and in forming our opinion thereon, and
        we do not provide a separate opinion on these matters. For each matter below, our description of
        how our audit addressed the matter is provided in that context.
